review_output: {"summary":"No BLOCKER found. The normal write path locks the version (share), then the visitor row, then inserts the visit and stales reports. That matches the version-then-report order used by report create/finish, so I see no deadlock cycle there. A late insert holds the version share lock, which blocks report-finish's version lock, so a finish that overlaps a late visit is correctly rejected or invalidated. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus the UPDATE guard means a replay cannot change a stored visitedAt. The main remaining risks: (1) For windows before the migration, the snapshot returns an 'available' empty visit list with no marker showing when visit facts actually started. (2) Millisecond truncation (date_trunc) versus rounding (TIMESTAMPTZ(3)) can wrongly reject a visit against firstVisitedAt or collectionStartedAt. (3) Replays fail once collection is disabled or expired, so they are not truly idempotent. (4) The delete/cascade path locks in the reverse order (visitor, then version) and requires read committed. (5) Per-row staling on bulk deletes is costly. (6) The trigger, conflict, staling and lock-order behaviour has no real-database tests.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"tests / migration verification","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visit.test.ts","issue":"The only tests mock $queryRaw by call position. Nothing checks the migration's real behaviour: the BEFORE INSERT guard firing on ON CONFLICT replays, the AFTER INSERT/DELETE staling of exactly the windows that contain a visit, the immutability guard, the read-committed checks, or the claimed lock order against report-create/finish.","evidence":"database([[], [{ id: \"version\" }], [{ id: \"visitor\" }], inserted ? [{ id: eventId }] : [], [{ visitedAt: new Date(1234) }]]) — all SQL is mocked; there is no test of LiveMetricVisit_guard or LiveMetricVisit_changed.","impact":"The migration's core correctness claims ('invalidates precisely the windows containing that visit', 'Share the version/report lock order', a replay keeps the first timestamp) are unverified. A wrong boundary operator or a missed status would silently allow stale ready reports.","recommended_fix":"Add Postgres integration tests for the migration and recordMetricVisit.","required_test":"Use a real database: (a) insert visits at windowStartAt and windowEndAt-1ms and at windowEndAt, and assert exactly which reports go stale; (b) run a concurrent report-finish and visit insert and assert that either finish is rejected or the result is cleared; (c) replay the same eventId after a delay and assert visitedAt is unchanged and replayed=true; (d) use the same eventId with a different visitor/tenant, assert rejection, and confirm no stale side effects; (e) assert UPDATE raises an error; (f) assert inserts under repeatable read fail.","confidence":0.8},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"timestamp precision","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visit.ts","issue":"visitedAt uses date_trunc('milliseconds', clock_timestamp()), which truncates. The comparison values firstVisitedAt and collectionStartedAt may come from clock_timestamp()/now() stored in TIMESTAMPTZ(3) columns, which round. If both events fall in the same millisecond, the truncated visitedAt can be up to 1ms earlier than the rounded firstVisitedAt, and the guard rejects a valid visit.","evidence":"VALUES (...,date_trunc('milliseconds',clock_timestamp())) vs guard: AND NEW.\"visitedAt\">=v.\"collectionStartedAt\" AND NEW.\"visitedAt\">=b.\"firstVisitedAt\"","impact":"A first visit recorded right after creating the visitor or enabling collection (for example in the same request or transaction) can fail with 23514 about half the time when both land in the same millisecond.","recommended_fix":"Use a single rounding rule. Either insert clock_timestamp()::timestamptz(3), which rounds the same way as the other columns, or compare against date_trunc('milliseconds', firstVisitedAt/collectionStartedAt). Also make sure visitor provisioning stores its timestamps the same way.","required_test":"Create a visitor and record a visit in the same transaction with firstVisitedAt fractional ms >= 0.5 (e.g. set firstVisitedAt = 'x.0006' before cast) and assert the visit is accepted.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"idempotence","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visit.ts","issue":"Postgres runs BEFORE INSERT triggers before the ON CONFLICT check. Once collection is disabled or the version expires, replaying an event that was already committed raises 'metric visit scope or lifetime invalid' instead of returning the original receipt. The same event ID therefore gives different results over time.","evidence":"// The insert guard checks collection/lifetime even on an idempotent replay. ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id","impact":"A client retrying after a lost response near expiry or disable gets an error for a visit that was actually recorded. The caller may count it as a failure or retry forever. The receipt API is not idempotent.","recommended_fix":"Within the visitor FOR UPDATE lock, first SELECT the existing visit for this scope and eventId. If it exists, return replayed=true with its stored visitedAt and skip the INSERT. Only insert when it is missing. Or document clearly that a replay after expiry returns an error.","required_test":"Record a visit, set collectionEnabled=false (or move expiresAt into the past), replay the same eventId, and assert the original visitedAtMs is returned with replayed=true. Or assert the documented error.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"historical completeness / provenance","file":"src/lib/live-metric-report-snapshot.ts","issue":"Visit facts only exist from the migration onward and are not backfilled. The report context still only exposes collectionStartedAt, which may be earlier than the migration. For any window that starts before visit facts existed, loadMetricViewingSnapshot returns status 'available' with visits: [], and nothing distinguishes that from a window with genuinely zero visits.","evidence":"Migration: 'Existing firstVisitedAt rows are not backfilled'. Reader context: { windowStartAt, windowEndAt, mode, durationMs, collectionEnabled, collectionStartedAt } — there is no visit-fact start marker. The snapshot initializes visits: [] and returns it as available.","impact":"A future calculation will undercount visits, or report zero, for pre-migration windows, even though the snapshot looks complete.","recommended_fix":"Record when visit facts started per version (e.g. a visitFactsStartedAt column set at migration time or when collection is enabled) and include it in MetricReportContext. Alternatively, have the reader return unavailable/incomplete when windowStartAt is earlier than it.","required_test":"For a version whose collectionStartedAt is earlier than the visit-fact start, request a report window spanning that start and assert the snapshot flags the visits as incomplete instead of returning an empty, complete list.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"lock order / deletion path","file":"prisma/migrations/20261014180000_live_metric_visits/migration.sql","issue":"Deleting a visitor (for example privacy erasure) or cascading from it locks in a different order from the comment's claim. The visitor row is locked first, then each cascaded visit's AFTER DELETE trigger takes the version FOR SHARE and then updates report rows. recordMetricVisit takes the version first, then the visitor. The two share locks don't conflict, so I don't see a cycle with today's create/finish paths. But any future path that takes the version FOR UPDATE and then touches the visitor (such as visitor provisioning or version disable with a visitor cleanup step) would deadlock against this.","evidence":"wp20_metric_visit_changed: PERFORM 1 FROM public.\"LiveMetricVersion\" ... FOR SHARE (executed after the cascade has locked LiveMetricVisitor); recordMetricVisit: version FOR SHARE then LiveMetricVisitor FOR UPDATE.","impact":"Deadlock aborts are possible when this is combined with future write paths. The 'shared lock order' comment is not true for deletions.","recommended_fix":"Document that deletes must first lock the version (FOR SHARE or stronger) before deleting a visitor or visits, and do that in the deletion code. Alternatively, drop the trigger's version lock when the caller already holds it.","required_test":"Run a visitor deletion concurrently with recordMetricVisit and report-create/finish. Assert there is no deadlock and that reports overlapping the deleted visits end up stale.","confidence":0.4},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"resource / cascades","file":"prisma/migrations/20261014180000_live_metric_visits/migration.sql","issue":"The AFTER DELETE trigger runs once per row and enforces read committed. A cascade that deletes a visitor or version with many visits re-locks the version and runs an UPDATE against LiveMetricReport for every visit. Any cascade started from a repeatable-read or serializable transaction fails outright, even for a version deletion where the trigger would just return NULL.","evidence":"CREATE TRIGGER \"LiveMetricVisit_changed\" AFTER INSERT OR DELETE ... FOR EACH ROW; the isolation check happens before IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN NULL.","impact":"Erasing a heavy visitor or deleting a version can be slow and lock-heavy, and it can't run inside a repeatable-read maintenance transaction. That makes privacy deletion fragile.","recommended_fix":"Use a statement-level AFTER DELETE trigger with a transition table (REFERENCING OLD TABLE), and stale each report window once using a set-based query. Check for a missing version before enforcing isolation, or allow the cascade case.","required_test":"Delete a visitor with 10k visits and assert bounded runtime and correct staling. Delete a version inside a repeatable-read transaction and assert it succeeds, or that the restriction is documented.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"tenant isolation / key design","file":"prisma/migrations/20261014180000_live_metric_visits/migration.sql","issue":"The event ID is a client-supplied UUID and is the global primary key across all vendors. A caller who reuses a UUID belonging to another tenant gets 'scope unavailable' instead of success. That leaks whether the UUID exists, and it permanently blocks the legitimate owner from using that ID if the attacker writes it first.","evidence":"id TEXT PRIMARY KEY ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING ... SELECT ... WHERE id=${request.eventId} AND \"vendorId\"=... → throw 'Metric visit scope unavailable'","impact":"A small cross-tenant existence oracle and possible squatting of known event IDs. The receipt correctly refuses to return another tenant's data.","recommended_fix":"Make the uniqueness key scoped, e.g. UNIQUE (vendorId, liveId, versionId, visitorId, id) with a server-generated surrogate primary key, and use that as the ON CONFLICT target.","required_test":"Insert the same eventId for two different vendors/visitors. Assert both succeed independently, and that neither affects the other's receipt or timestamp.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"NIT","area":"concurrency","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visit.ts","issue":"The visitor row is locked FOR UPDATE, which conflicts with the FOR KEY SHARE locks that foreign-key checks take in other tables referencing LiveMetricVisitor (and in this table's own FK). FOR NO KEY UPDATE is enough to serialize retries.","evidence":"SELECT id FROM \"LiveMetricVisitor\" WHERE ... FOR UPDATE","impact":"Needless blocking of concurrent inserts into tables that reference the visitor, and more room for lock interactions.","recommended_fix":"Use FOR NO KEY UPDATE.","required_test":"Insert a row that references the visitor via FK while a visit transaction holds the lock, and assert it is not blocked.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"NIT","area":"schema consistency","file":"prisma/migrations/20261014180000_live_metric_visits/migration.sql","issue":"The FK declares ON UPDATE CASCADE, but the guard rejects every UPDATE on LiveMetricVisit, and visitor keys are immutable. TRUNCATE is not covered by the DELETE trigger, so it would skip report staling.","evidence":"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE; IF TG_OP='UPDATE' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'metric visit facts are immutable'","impact":"Contradictory declarations. A privileged TRUNCATE would leave ready reports computed from facts that no longer exist.","recommended_fix":"Use ON UPDATE NO ACTION/RESTRICT. Add a BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger that raises an error, or one that stales all affected reports.","required_test":"Assert that TRUNCATE \"LiveMetricVisit\" is rejected or stales the reports.","confidence":0.6}]}
